definition: The task of identifying and classifying named entities (such as people, organizations, locations, or dates) within text.
details: Entity extraction (a form of Named Entity Recognition) is a foundational NLP task used in applications ranging from information retrieval to building knowledge graphs from unstructured text.

explainer.lead: Entity extraction turns mentions of things like people, organizations, locations, and dates in ordinary text into labeled pieces of data. This makes unstructured writing easier to search, organize, and connect.

tiers.eli5: Imagine reading a story with different colored highlighters: pink for people, blue for companies, and green for places. Entity extraction teaches a computer to do that highlighting and write down what each highlighted phrase represents.
tiers.practitioner: In practice, entity extraction converts text into entity spans with labels such as person, organization, location, or date. These outputs can feed information retrieval or knowledge graph construction; clear entity categories and consistent span boundaries are important when integrating the results.
tiers.paperLevel: Given input text T, entity extraction produces a set E = {(s_i, l_i)}, where each s_i is a text span and l_i is its entity category, such as person, organization, location, or date. It is therefore a structured prediction task over both entity boundaries and labels.

explainer.example: For “Maria joined Acme in Paris on 3 May,” the output could label “Maria” as a person, “Acme” as an organization, “Paris” as a location, and “3 May” as a date.

usedIn.name: Information retrieval
usedIn.detail: Labeled people, organizations, locations, and dates provide structured information extracted from text.

usedIn.name: Knowledge graph construction
usedIn.detail: Extracted entities supply named things that can be represented from unstructured text.

explainer.intuition: Instead of treating a sentence as only a sequence of words, entity extraction picks out the phrases that name specific kinds of things and records their categories.
howItWorks: Identify text spans that mention named entities.
Assign each span a category such as person, organization, location, or date.
Return the entity text, its category, and its position in the input.
explainer.whyItMatters: It provides a bridge from unstructured text to structured entity records. That foundation supports information retrieval and the construction of knowledge graphs.
misconceptions: It does more than find keywords: it identifies entity spans and assigns entity categories.
The task labels mentions in text; the definition does not itself require linking them to records in a knowledge graph.

diagram.caption: Entity extraction turns unstructured text into labeled entity spans.
